# How much syndrome information must become irreversible?

Author: `producer-workspace/classical_capacity`, 29 October 2026. New construction; independent review is separate. The accepted `p2_protection` results remain unchanged. This is a theorem about an acquired completed quantum instrument, not a circuit threshold, entropy-production bound or implemented device advantage.

## 1. Consequence and precise interface

Distance-order suppression does not require making the entire error syndrome classical. After **coherent correction using the full fine syndrome**, only a bounded fault-weight tier must lose its coherence. For a code correcting the acquired fault set through order t, at most **t+1 irreversible sectors** suffice for order d=2t+1, even when the complete fine syndrome remains a quantum output. For odd phase repetition codes this number is optimal for nondemolition syndrome-diagonal conversion. Imperfect conversion has a graded requirement: coherence between tiers separated by Delta can first hurt at order d-Delta, so overlap O(eta^Delta) restores order d.

The mathematical operation retains the logical output, the complete fine syndrome S, all actual classical detector/receiver records, and all quantum memory B that can return. Any subsystem traced in the converter must remain outside every later admitted interaction. A purification which later returns belongs in B/O from the beginning. No marginal calibration law, unread key average or temporarily inaccessible environment establishes that boundary.

Source encoding, syndrome extraction, coherent lookup/correction and the converter are acquired operations. Added source-control noise, direct contact with unprocessed source-imprinted fields, leakage, loss, capture and later reset require their own completed interfaces and budgets. A known logical target has been removed in its correct output frame. The theorem does not construct a compatible gate or an efficient decoder.

# Exact closed couplers preserve circuit fault support

Author: `producer-workspace/architecture_challenge`, 29 October 2026. New construction and executable challenge; independent review is separate. Nothing in `p2_protection` is modified or receives a new review by this author.

## 1. Consequence and acquired interface

An unreset mediator need not turn one physical fault into faults at every later gate. A gate that closes on its **whole admitted mediator space** can be substituted into an ordinary fault-tolerant circuit while preserving its fault-location support. This gives a reusable interaction resource, including for syndrome circuits with noisy quantum controls. It preserves the protections of the chosen conventional circuit; it does not supply a new error-correcting code or make a shared syndrome meter intrinsically safe.

Let D be all source qubits, M the reused controlled mediator, and E any uncontrolled quantum memory. An abstract two-qubit gate j has source support A_j={a_j,b_j}. Its physical macro contains only operations on A_j and M. Its fault-free completed action is U_j=G_j tensor I_M. Free bath evolution on E can be included. Arbitrary M,E-only evolution may occur between macros. Initial M and E may be mixed and correlated with D and an external reference. They need not be prepared, measured or reset between good macros.

The native ports used below are controlled-X and controlled-Z from any selected source endpoint to M, calibrated source Hadamards, native source Paulis, and actual source-ancilla preparation and Z measurement/readout. The source endpoints include data, syndrome meters and flags. The controller chooses actual gates and retains all classical results. Addressing/lookup logic is trusted; quantum pulses, preparation, measurement and readout can be faulty.

Inside a macro a contact fault may be an arbitrary completed operation on its active source endpoint, M and E. A source-only control fault may act on that source and E. An inactive-source idle fault may act on that source and E, but must not directly couple the idle source to M. Ideal contact pulses act trivially on E; bath-only E evolution can be put in an interaction frame. These support conditions are substantive. # Reusable closure, local coherent faults, and causal normalization

Author `producer-workspace/protected_algebra`, 29 October 2026. New work in `p2_reuse`; all `p2_protection` predecessors remain frozen. This is an authored theorem package, not its independent review or a hardware threshold certificate.

## 1. Consequence and interface

A mediator can retain arbitrary quantum memory between completed operations without becoming an uncontrolled broadcast path for an old fault. The decisive condition is that every *good completed operation*, on its entire admitted returning-memory input, acts as the intended data operation tensor a memory operation. Every later transfer of the bath's stored information back to new data must then pay another local fault factor. No bath reset, short correlation time, commuting bath coefficients, or small bath-only Hamiltonian is required **between those boundaries**.

This statement concerns a declared network of ports. A boundary is not created merely by naming a pulse sequence a gate. It must include all returning carriers, coherently selected controls, actual records and continuation after leakage/loss. A retained classical record that later controls the intended computation is a computational control rail: its corruption is a charged control fault, not unrestricted bath-only evolution. Internal interfaces exposed to outside intervention must be additional declared boundaries, each with its own theorem. A small completed-call channel distance supplies no arbitrary-intervention guarantee inside the call.

Three constructions are proved here:

1. A finite observable-algebra test acquires an approximate product dilation on all returning-memory states, with no bath-dimension factor. For an actual unitary, a uniform reduced-data channel certificate also gives a **linear** conversion. The stronger uniform input promise is essential.
2. Product closure plus physical support gives the usual selected-location coherent-noise condition, even under arbitrary noncommuting bath evolution between macros. Unselected operations are resummed as actual contractions; no factor exponential in computation volume is incurred.
